subject: presence of a real mobile phone in frame
why: The moments table is NOT ground truth. Every row in it with kind='MOBILE_DEVICE' is a
detector OUTPUT — the thing under test — so scoring the detector against it scores the
detector against its own opinion. Nine of these twenty-five frames contain no phone at
all; they are the over-ear headset and shadowed-face-edge false positives the lower-tile
pass produced. A harness that reads the moments table as truth therefore rewards the bug
and reports the fix for it as a 36% recall regression.
So the labels live here instead, in a file a human can open and argue with. 'verified'
means a person looked at the pixels and said so. It is the difference between a number
that means something and a number that only looks like it does.
how_to_add: Run bench_phone_validate.py --sheet. It renders every frame with the box drawn and a
#N caption. Look at each one, then set phone_present and flip verified to true. Frames
left unverified are excluded from the scores rather than guessed at — an unlabelled
frame is a frame nobody has checked, and averaging over guesses is how the moments
table got trusted in the first place.

frames.note: Real phone, held in hand, confirmed by review — and the full-frame pass scores 0.000 on it. Not 'just under the floor': there is no box at all, so no threshold anywhere recovers this one. It sits in the moments table only because the deleted lower-tile pass caught it, which makes it the single genuine regression from removing the tiles. This is the frame that justifies the native-720p capture path: the sweep currently downscales a 1280x720 capture to 640x360 before sending, and this phone does not survive that.
